original_question: For the antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX spin chain, consider ground-state correlation functions of local spin operators on sequential lattice sites, including quantities such as the emptiness formation probability. These correlation functions are known to be expressible as polynomials in ln 2 and in values of the Riemann zeta function, or equivalently the alternating zeta series, at odd arguments with rational coefficients. Find an efficient and tractable description of the rational coefficients that appear in these polynomial expressions.
target_in_paper: Section 2.3, the open problem stated immediately after Conjecture 1: "Efficient description of the rational coefficients which appear in the expression for the correlation functions of the XXX spin chain as a polynomial in alternating zeta series at odd arguments."
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct model (the antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX chain), the correct class of observables in substance (ground-state local correlation functions on consecutive sites, including emptiness formation probability), the correct arithmetic structure (polynomials with rational coefficients in ln 2 and odd zeta values, equivalently alternating zeta values at odd arguments), and the correct mathematical target: not proving polynomiality itself, but finding an efficient/tractable description of the rational coefficients. That is exactly the open problem posed after the paper recalls Conjecture 1 and the later proof of polynomiality.
missing_details: The paper works with the infinite-chain Hamiltonian H_XXX = sum_{j=-∞}^{∞}(σ_j^xσ_{j+1}^x + σ_j^yσ_{j+1}^y + σ_j^zσ_{j+1}^z) and its unique antiferromagnetic ground state |GS> in the thermodynamic limit.
A correlation function is defined precisely as <GS|prod_{k=1}^n σ_k^{a_k}|GS>, where the sites are n consecutive lattice sites and each local factor is chosen from {σ_k^0, σ_k^x, σ_k^y, σ_k^z}.
The emptiness formation probability is explicitly P(n) = <GS|prod_{j=1}^n P_j|GS>, where P_j = (σ_j^z + 1)/2 is the projector onto spin-up at site j.

The paper phrases the open problem in the alternating-zeta basis ζ_a(1), ζ_a(3), ζ_a(5), ...; the ln 2 / odd-ζ formulation is equivalent only after using ζ_a(1) = ln 2 and ζ(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})^{-1}ζ_a(s) for s != 1.
The quantifier should be explicit: the coefficient-description is sought for every such local correlator, i.e. for all n and all choices of local operators on consecutive sites.
The ambient coefficient field should be stated explicitly as Q: the issue is to describe the rational coefficients in the Q-polynomial expansions.

No extra homogeneity, degree bound, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic qualifier is part of this paper's formulation; the question should stay narrowly on local XXX-chain correlators and their arithmetic coefficients.
refined_question: For the infinite antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX chain with Hamiltonian H_XXX = sum_{j=-∞}^{∞}(σ_j^xσ_{j+1}^x + σ_j^yσ_{j+1}^y + σ_j^zσ_{j+1}^z), let |GS> be its unique ground state in the thermodynamic limit, and for any n consecutive sites define a local correlation function by C_{a_1,...,a_n} = <GS|prod_{k=1}^n σ_k^{a_k}|GS>, where each σ_k^{a_k} belongs to {σ_k^0, σ_k^x, σ_k^y, σ_k^z}; in particular, P(n) = <GS|prod_{j=1}^n ((σ_j^z+1)/2)|GS> is the emptiness formation probability. Since these correlators are known to be expressible as polynomials over Q in the alternating zeta values ζ_a(1), ζ_a(3), ζ_a(5), ... , can one give an efficient and tractable description of the rational coefficients appearing in those polynomial expressions for arbitrary n and arbitrary choices of the local operators?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent, using ζ_a(1) = ln 2 and ζ(s) = (1 - 2^{1-s})^{-1}ζ_a(s) for s != 1: can one efficiently describe the rational coefficients in the expression of every local XXX-chain ground-state correlation function as a polynomial over Q in ln 2 and the odd Riemann zeta values ζ(3), ζ(5), ζ(7), ... ?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's first open problem in Section 2.3, not merely Conjecture 1. Conjecture 1 records the polynomiality statement, but the paper then says that this conjecture was proved and immediately isolates the remaining issue as an open problem: describing the rational coefficients efficiently. Your draft already captures that distinction correctly. The refinement mainly makes the question fully stand-alone by importing the exact Hamiltonian/ground-state setting from Section 2, the precise definition of the class of correlation functions from Section 2.1, the exact definition of emptiness formation probability, the Q-polynomial ambient ring, and the paper's preferred alternating-zeta formulation together with the explicit equivalence to the ln 2 and odd-zeta formulation from Section 2.2.
